 Dated this the 13th day of September, 2024
 Order
Anil K. Narendran, J. 
The Cochin Devaswom Board has filed this writ petition seeking a writ of certiorari to quash Exts.P1,
P3, P4 and P6 and for a declaration that the provisions contained in the Legal Metrology Act, 2009,
and the Food and Safety Standards Act, 2006 do not apply to the prasadam/offering in a temple/religious institutions and to direct respondents 7 and 8 to close the proceedings initiated pursuant to Exts.P1, P3, P4 and P6.
2. The issue raised in this writ petition is in respect of 'Neypayasam', in Chottanikkara Bhagavathy Temple, which is a temple under the management of Cochin Devaswom Board. In the writ petition,
it is stated that one among the 'nivedya vazhipadu' in Chottanikkara Bhagavathy Temple is 'Neypayasam'. 
3. Admit.
4. The learned Deputy Solicitor General of India-in- charge enters appearance for the 1st respondent Union of India, Adv. Chitra P. George, the learned Standing Counsel for Food Safety and Standards Authority of India for the 2nd respondent and the learned Senior Government Pleader for respondents 3 to 8.
5. During the course of arguments, the learned Standing Counsel for Cochin Devaswom Board would point out the decisions of a Division Bench of this Court in Travancore Devaswom Board v.
Ayyappa Spices [2023 (4) KHC SN 9: 2023 KHC OnLine 286] and Ayyappa Spices v. Travancore Devaswom Board [2023:KER:24739 : 2023 KHC OnLine 9678] and also the decision of the Apex Court in Travancore Devaswom Board v. Ayyappa Spices [2024 (2) KHC SN 5: 2024 SCC OnLine SC 244]. The learned Standing Counsel would submit that while setting aside the aforesaid decisions of Cochin Devaswom Board vs Union Of India on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83066253/
2 this Court on the question of maintainability of a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the Apex Court observed that issue No.2 relating to the applicability of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, to the Travancore Devaswom Board does not arise for consideration in that case.
6. The learned Deputy Solicitor General on India-in- charge, the learned Standing Counsel for Food Safety and Standards Authority of India and the learned Senior Government Pleader seeks time to file counter affidavits. Four weeks' time granted. 
7. There will be an interim stay as prayed for, for a period of one month. 
List on 11.10.2024. 
Sd/-
ANIL K. NARENDRAN, JUDGE Sd/-
